title: add-vpc-control-plane-provisioning-multi-az-subnets-endpoints-sgs-peering-dns-terraform
author: Asha Kapoor
description: Motivation: Add Terraform provisioning for the Private Control Plane VPC to support multi-AZ deployments and standard networking components required by our Private deployment mode. This includes: multi-AZ public/private subnets, interface and gateway endpoints for AWS services (S3, ECR, Secrets Manager, STS), security group rules and templates for control-plane <> customer VPC peering, Route53 private hosted zone automation, and helper outputs for the installer. The change is split across a reusable terraform module (terraform/modules/vpc-control-plane) and the installer integration (terraform/envs/private-control-plane). Checklist: - [x] Add reusable VPC control plane module with inputs for AZs, cidr ranges, endpoint toggles - [x] Create Route53 private hosted zone module and automatic delegation records for peering setups - [x] Implement interface endpoint creation for required AWS services and allow-list security groups - [x] Add VPC peering provisioning + cross-account role guidance notes - [x] Add integration tests (terraform validate/plan) and basic acceptance tests in CI - [x] Update installer README and upgrade/rollback notes - [x] Run manual validation in staging with a 3-AZ customer VPC Summary of changes: - New module: terraform/modules/vpc-control-plane (main.tf, variables.tf, outputs.tf, README.md) - New module: terraform/modules/route53-private-zone (main.tf, records.tf) - Env overlay: terraform/envs/private-control-plane/main.tf and variables.tf - Installer docs: docs/private/vpc-control-plane.md and docs/upgrade-rollback.md - CI: .github/workflows/terraform-private-control-plane.yml - Tests: infra/tests/vpc_control_plane_acceptance_test.sh Notes and rationale: - We standardize on interface endpoints where possible to reduce NAT/eip surface and to make Private deployments compatible with restrictive customer network policies. S3 uses gateway endpoint when the customer VPC CIDR allows it; otherwise we default to interface endpoint and document tradeoffs. - Security groups are generated with least-privilege ingress rules for control-plane APIs and a named set of "installer-managed" groups so customers can reference them. - Route53 private hosted zone is created in the control-plane account and delegation records are written to the customer VPC when peering is enabled; we include an optional manual step for cross-account delegation in highly regulated setups. Upgrade and rollback: - Upgrades are safe if you follow the documented plan: apply new module outputs referencing existing subnets first, then create endpoints, then update security groups. - Rollback guidance includes explicit Terraform state steps and enforcement of a safe order to avoid DNS blips (create hostnames in new zone before switching delegation). Security review: - KMS usage is opt-in and scoped; secrets remain in customer-managed Secrets Manager by default. - No plaintext credentials are added; IAM role templates are provided for cross-account peering only when required. Migration/compatibility: - Existing single-AZ setups are supported via variables (az_count = 1 by default) so this module is backward compatible. - We added deprecation notes for the legacy vpc_control_plane module in README.

release_notes: Add reusable terraform modules to provision Private Control Plane VPC: multi-AZ subnets, interface/gateway endpoints, security groups, VPC peering automation, and Route53 private hosted zone delegation. Installer docs updated with upgrade and rollback guidance. Backwards compatible with single-AZ installs (set az_count=1).
notes_for_ops: Staging validation performed against a 3-AZ customer VPC. When applying in production, follow docs/private/vpc-control-plane.md: ensure state locking, apply provider aliases for cross-account resources, and follow the upgrade plan (subnets -> endpoints -> security groups -> DNS delegation). Rollback requires manual Terraform state manipulation documented in docs/upgrade-rollback.md.
